name: subagents
description: How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
---

Subagents are **your team's workers**: focused helpers you (the team lead) spawn
to divide up review and upkeep while you keep proving. This is delegation
*within* your team and needs no permission — distinct from launching new tasks or
runs for *other* teams, which is off by default (see the `horizon` skill,
"Delegating beyond your team"). The `ground` helper is the fresh-context
checkpoint for workspace-wide strategy and hygiene; it is a subagent, not a
second orchestrator role.

Bundled descriptors and any workspace overrides under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` are merged at the start of every `horizon
run`, then compiled into your engine's **native** subagent format,
workspace-local:

- Claude Code → `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- Codex → `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`

Use the engine's native roster, or list `.codex/agents/*.toml` for Codex and
`.claude/agents/*.md` for Claude, to see every runnable helper. Do not treat an
empty `.archon-horizon/subagents/` directory as an empty roster: that directory
holds workspace overrides/custom helpers only; built-ins such as `ground`,
`janitor`, and `work-reviewer` still appear in the compiled native directory.
Pick the right helper and scope from those generated descriptions.

## Dispatch

Spawn a subagent **by name** through your engine's own native subagent
mechanism, with a focused directive: the slice/scope (a chapter, a task, a
project) and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work
divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Give one subagent
one scoped slice so the workspace scales to many projects.

Delegation is part of the normal workflow, not an exceptional recovery path.
For a session that touches more than one file, more than one proof obligation,
or is expected to run longer than ten minutes, dispatch at least one bounded
review/helper before the final report. On a multi-session task, dispatch
`ground` before the terminal completion claim and `janitor` at the scheduled
hygiene checkpoints. Use the engine's native `spawn_agent`/Task mechanism,
wait for the helper to finish, and reconcile its report in your own result. If
no suitable helper is available, state why delegation was skipped in the report.

## Read-only and write scope

A descriptor's `read_only: true` is compiled to real engine enforcement — Claude
`disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`, Codex `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`
— so a read-only reviewer cannot edit source. Every subagent (read-only or not)
can still file issues/memory and write its report via the `horizon inbox` CLI;
that is how read-only agents act. The descriptor's `write_domain` documents what
a writer is expected to touch (Lean/blueprint/reference source).

## Model and effort — the Horizon agent owns the spend

Descriptors intentionally carry no model, tier, or effort setting. Generated
Claude/Codex descriptors inherit the parent session by default. At dispatch time,
the Horizon agent chooses the native model and reasoning effort for that helper:
use the same model/effort for mathematical review, a lighter capable option for
mechanical search/lint/hygiene, and a vision-capable option for page transcription.
If the engine cannot express a per-call override, inherit the parent and record
the choice in the report rather than hiding a model policy in `config.yaml`.

The same rule applies to a named subagent, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or any
workflow fan-out. Match model and effort to the actual slice, and before a large
fan-out check `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. If headroom is low, commit work in
flight first so an interruption loses nothing.

To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run. Do not rely on a
stale hard-coded roster in this skill.

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor.       "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient \u27e8sorry\u27e9` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION




LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN
FORMALIZATION
Complete Recovery and Execution Plan

AJCR-first strategy for Picard representability, Galois descent, and final Jacobian
construction




Version: 1.0
Date: August 2026
Primary endpoint: Kernel-checked arbitrary-field Pic^0 representability
Secondary endpoint: JacobianData constructed from the same pinned representation




Working principle
Progress is measured by closed theorem dependencies, consumed producers, deleted obsolete
paths, and kernel-checked endpoints - not by raw LOC growth.




                                                                                       Page 1
 LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION



Contents
  1. Executive summary
  2. The three principal issues
  3. Binding architecture decision
  4. Definition of success
  5. Phase 0 - Freeze, measure, and establish the critical root
  6. Phase 1 - Lock the endgame contract and route guards
  7. Phase 2 - Cap the parameter-decoupling lane
  8. Phase 3 - Repair type and instance mismatches
  9. Phase 4 - Construct the rank-one Picard chart
  10. Phase 5 - Cover over a separably closed field
  11. Phase 6 - Produce Pic^0 over the separable closure
  12. Phase 7 - Complete finite Galois descent
  13. Phase 8 - Construct the final Jacobian witness
  14. AJC integration strategy
  15. Eight-round execution schedule
  16. Agent roles and dispatch specifications
  17. Merge, credit, and stop rules
  18. Progress dashboard and acceptance tests
  19. Risk register and fallback decisions
  20. Immediate action list
  Appendix A. Suggested theorem signatures
  Appendix B. Minimal dependency graph


1. Executive summary
The project has made real progress, especially in widened divisor-family infrastructure, rank calculations,
and finite-Galois descent machinery. However, the current code growth does not yet correspond to
comparable movement toward the final Picard representability theorem. The central reason is architectural:
large divisor degree gives coverage but destroys Abel-map injectivity, while genus degree gives rank-one
uniqueness but is harder to cover over an arbitrary base field.

The recommended route is therefore AJCR-first and follows the curve-specialized classical construction:
build a rank-one Picard open over a separably closed field, represent it by an open inside the degree-g
divisor scheme, cover the Picard functor by translations of this open, then descend the resulting Pic^0
through finite Galois descent. AJC should be used as the shared descent engine and long-term infrastructure
project rather than as a second independent Picard proof.

  Primary decision
  The next endpoint-critical theorem is the family-level natural isomorphism between the rank-one open
  inside Div^g and the rank-one open inside the Picard functor. Parameter decoupling remains useful
  infrastructure, but it is no longer the main Picard endpoint lane.


The complete execution plan below is organized around one dependency chain:


                                                                                                      Page 2
 LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION



    PicRankOneOpen
        -> rankOneAbelIso
        -> rankOne_translate_cover_sepClosed
        -> pic0_sepClosed_representableBy
        -> finiteGaloisDescent
        -> pic0_representableBy
        -> JacobianData




2. The three principal issues
2.1 Coverage degree and injectivity degree are incompatible
On a genus-g curve, a nonspecial divisor of degree n has h^0 = n + 1 - g. At a sufficiently large admissible
degree, coverage is available, but h^0 is greater than 1 in positive genus. The Abel map then has positive-
dimensional linear-system fibres and cannot directly be the monomorphism or open immersion required by
the existing Picard chart seam.

At degree n = g, the same rank formula gives h^0 = 1 on the nonspecial locus, so uniqueness and an open-
immersion chart become possible. However, the required degree-g translation data need not exist over an
arbitrary base field. The project has therefore been attempting to make two different parameter regimes
solve one seam.

    Parameter regime                   What it gives                       What fails

    n=g                                Rank-one fibres; potential open     Pointwise coverage over the original
                                       immersion                           base field

    n = admissible > g                 Uniform coverage and large-degree   Injectivity; the Abel fibres have h^0 >
                                       control                             1




2.2 Lean interfaces are hiding mathematical misalignment
Several classifier layers use one symbol for distinct semantic roles: curve genus, divisor degree, and window
parameters. Equivalent geometric objects are also represented by different Lean expressions, causing
expensive definitional-equality and typeclass-search failures. Weak existential witnesses and source/test-
locus mismatches have allowed locally true lemmas to accumulate without closing the intended producer.

      Hard-coded diagonal relation n = g in classifier and RepresentableBy layers.
      Repeated transports between relCurve-style and explicit base-change expressions.
      Duplicate diagonal and generalized proofs surviving in parallel.
      Fieldwise uniqueness results used where the consumer needs a natural inverse on arbitrary test
       schemes.
      Compatibility wrappers that move hypotheses but do not create the missing geometric map.

2.3 The final theorem chain is not yet closed
The repository contains many strong components, but the final path is still discontinuous. The missing
central theorem is not another rank or coverage lemma; it is a family-level identification of the correct
divisor open with the correct Picard open, followed by a complete descent theorem returning both the
descended scheme and its RepresentableBy certificate.




                                                                                                             Page 3
 LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION



    Diagnostic rule
    A theorem is endpoint progress only when it is root-reachable and consumed by the next declaration on
    the critical path. An unconsumed alias, wrapper, generalized lemma, or isolated proof is infrastructure
    inventory.




3. Binding architecture decision
3.1 Chosen route
Use the curve-specialized rank-one atlas over a separably closed field, then descend. The binding route is:

    rank-one open inside Div^g
        <-> rank-one Picard open
        -> translated open cover over k^s
        -> Pic^0 represented over k^s
        -> finite Galois descent
        -> Pic^0 represented over k




3.2 Role of the high-degree divisor lane
Complete one useful vertical arbitrary-degree representability spine, then freeze broad propagation unless a
named downstream theorem consumes it. This work remains valuable for divisor geometry, Brill-Noether
theory, projective-bundle descriptions, and a possible quotient fallback, but it should not be counted as
direct completion of the old Picard open-chart seam.

3.3 When a quotient route may be reconsidered
A large-degree Abel quotient should be reopened only after a non-circular Lean-shaped theorem contract is
written. The contract must construct a scheme quotient, prove its universal property, prove base-change
compatibility, and produce the desired map to the Picard functor without assuming Picard representability.
Merely defining equality of induced Picard class is not sufficient.


4. Definition of success
The project is complete only when the same pinned representability datum is consumed all the way to the
Jacobian witness.

    noncomputable def pic0_representableBy :
        Sigma fun J : Scheme => (pic0Functor C).RepresentableBy J


    noncomputable def jacobianData :
        JacobianData C



The final verification must include:

     Both declarations imported by the narrow critical-path root and the full project root.
     Axiom audit showing no project-specific axioms or sorryAx.
     Group structure, universal element, base change, and cocycle coherence derived from the same
      representation rather than separately chosen objects.


                                                                                                         Page 4
 LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION


      AJC either consumes this representability engine or formally derives its own producer from the shared
       implementation.


5. Phase 0 - Freeze, measure, and establish the critical root
5.1 Pin reproducible revisions
1.     Pin the last commit before the major LOC increase.
2.     Pin current main.
3.     Pin the latest committed state of parameter-decoupling run 0108.
4.     Pin the latest committed state of rank/index run 0109.

5.2 Build the baseline ledger
For each revision, measure the items below. The numbers must be generated from scripts and recorded with
the exact commit hash.

    Measurement                                            Purpose

    Root-reachable modules                                 Exclude dead scratch lanes from progress claims

    Root-reachable sorry/axioms                            Measure kernel status on the actual path

    Old DivFamZar consumers                                Verify that migration removes the old architecture

    New DivFamZarAff consumers                             Measure adoption outside the implementation cone

    Critical-path declarations                             Measure theorem movement rather than file growth

    Heartbeat/depth overrides                              Detect proof-term and elaboration deterioration

    Critical-root time and peak memory                     Measure iteration speed

    Full-root build status                                 Catch duplicate declarations and hidden imports




5.3 Create a narrow critical-path root
    -- Picard/Pic0CriticalPath.lean
    import ...DivRepChartClassUnivAffRepresentable
    import ...Pic0ChartLocusH0Rank
    import ...Pic0RankOneOpen
    import ...Pic0RepresentabilityFinal


    #check divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy
    #check rankOneAbelIso
    #check pic0_sepClosed_representableBy
    #check pic0_representableBy




5.4 Acceptance criteria
      The baseline can be reproduced by another person from the pinned commits.
      Every endpoint declaration is checked in the narrow root.
      A theorem proved in isolation receives no critical-path credit until imported here.




                                                                                                                Page 5
 LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION



6. Phase 1 - Lock the endgame contract and route guards
6.1 Create the contract file
Create Picard/Pic0EndgameContract.lean. The statements must elaborate even if some proofs temporarily
depend on explicit local hypotheses. Every declaration must list its exact mathematical source, Lean
prerequisites, and immediate consumer.

    def PicRankOneOpen : ...
    def DivRankOneOpen : ...
    def rankOneAbel : ...
    def divisorOfRankOne : ...


    theorem rankOneAbelIso : ...
    theorem rankOne_translate_cover_sepClosed : ...


    noncomputable def pic0_sepClosed_representableBy : ...
    noncomputable def pic0_representableBy : ...




6.2 Add a route guard against the false high-degree seam
Assemble a root-imported negative theorem showing that, in positive genus and at parameter n > g, the
unrestricted Abel map cannot be the desired open immersion because its fibres have at least two sections.
This theorem prevents future agents from accidentally treating the admissible divisor producer as direct
completion of the old chart seam.

6.3 Acceptance criteria
        The endpoint appears as one short dependency graph with no hidden route fork.
        High-degree divisor representability is clearly labeled infrastructure.
        Any quotient proposal must first replace the binding architecture decision with a complete theorem
         contract.


7. Phase 2 - Cap the parameter-decoupling lane
7.1 Separate semantic parameters
    Name                                 Meaning                             Permitted use

    gC                                   Genus of the curve                  Euler characteristic, Riemann-Roch,
                                                                             cohomological bounds

    nDiv                                 Degree represented by the divisor   DivFamZarAff, certified families, divisor
                                         functor                             scheme degree

    mWin                                 Lower window index                  Window construction only

    sWin                                 Window width                        Window construction only

    r1, r2                               Ranks of section modules            Bases and Grassmannian data

    m, Z                                 Abel translation/index data         Chart value and degree calibration




                                                                                                                  Page 6

LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION



7.2 Complete one vertical spine
Work top-down from the desired producer. Generalize only declarations reached by type errors on one
complete path; do not pre-generalize the entire library.

    noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_at
        (gC nDiv : Nat)
        (hchi : chi O_C = 1 - gC) :
        Sigma fun D => (divFunctorAff C nDiv).RepresentableBy D



Then define both the genus and admissible producers as specializations. The old diagonal proof must be
deleted or reduced to a one-line specialization.

7.3 Mandatory regression tests
     Diagonal test: nDiv = gC.
     Off-diagonal test: nDiv = admissibleCoverageParameter C.
     Next-consumer test: the generalized producer is actually used by a downstream theorem.

7.4 Stop condition
After the arbitrary-degree producer lands, freeze broad parameter propagation unless a named theorem
consumes it. Do not spend further rounds generalizing unused layers.


8. Phase 3 - Repair type and instance mismatches
8.1 Canonicalize base-changed curves
Choose one public spelling, preferably relCurve C L, throughout the critical path. Place all identifications
with explicit tensor/base-change expressions in one bridge module.

    -- Curve/RelativeCurveBridge.lean
    -- canonical isomorphisms
    -- transported instances
    -- inferInstanceAs bridges
    -- base-change simp lemmas




8.2 Build minimal performance regressions
Isolate each identity-like application that currently requires extreme heartbeat or recursion settings. The
refactor is complete only when the reproducer compiles under the normal budget.

8.3 Add semantic anti-vacuity tests
     Every existential witness must explicitly recover or represent the input Picard class.
     A zero or unrelated divisor must not satisfy the conclusion accidentally.
     Field-level uniqueness must not be credited as a natural inverse on arbitrary test schemes.

8.4 Acceptance criteria
     Critical files use one public curve spelling.
     Casts and instance transports are concentrated in the bridge module.
     No new parallel high-priority instances are introduced.

                                                                                                           Page 7
 LEAN ALGEBRAIC JACOBIAN FORMALIZATION


     The regression examples compile without enlarged global limits.


9. Phase 4 - Construct the rank-one Picard chart
9.1 Define one public rank-one Picard open
For a test scheme T and f_T : C_T -> T, define the open subfunctor consisting of line bundles L such that R^1
f_* L = 0 and f_* L is locally free of rank one, with the required base-change compatibility. This should be the
single public notion of the good Picard locus.

    def PicRankOneOpen :
        Subfunctor (picFunctor C)



Existing chartLocus, H0Rank, and H1-vanishing predicates must become implementation lemmas or be
proved equivalent to this definition.

3. Why the blocker is mathematically the right one
At a mathematical level, the gap is exactly the passage from pointwise/fibrewise information to a family
construction. Knowing that a line bundle has h0 = 1 and H1 = 0 after passing to fields is not, by itself,
enough to define the inverse Abel construction as a morphism on arbitrary test schemes.
   To construct a relative effective divisor canonically from a family of line bundles, the pushforward must
    behave as a rank-one locally free object on the relevant locus, not merely have one-dimensional fibres.
   The construction must commute with pullback. In Lean terms, the cartesian pushforward/base-change
    morphisms needed by the public API have to be IsIso in the precise hypotheses used by the family.
   The H0 rank-one statement and H1 vanishing must be tied to the same native presentation and
    transported coherently under arbitrary affine base change.
   Only then does the canonical section/evaluation divisor vary functorially and supply the inverse to the Abel
    map on the rank-one open locus.

    representability/open-locus theorem. This is precisely why run 123 is correct to refuse that shortcut.

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

    12	/-!
    13	# The lambda-tied datum underlying a native rank-one presentation
    14	
    15	Every affine Picard value is represented on an etale cover. This file exposes that actual
    16	representative and refines its relative Picard class to a basic-open cocycle datum. The output is
    17	tied to the displayed value; it makes no cohomology, rank, evaluation-divisor, or base-change
    18	claim.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    27	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    32	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    33	
    34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    35	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    37	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    38	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    39	
    40	/--
    41	The part of a native presentation forced by the displayed Picard value.
    42	
    43	`represents` ties the etale-plus representative to `lam`, while `datum_class` ties the
    44	basic-open cocycle datum to that same representative. The geometric certificates that enrich
    45	this datum are intentionally absent.
    46	-/
    47	structure PicRankOneNativeDatum
    48	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    49	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    50	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    51	  represents :
    52	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    53	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    54	  datum_class :
    55	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    56	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    57	
    58	namespace PicRankOneNativeDatum
    59	
    60	/-- Every displayed affine Picard value has a tied basic-open cocycle datum.
    61	
    62	The proof exposes an etale-plus representative of the displayed value, chooses a Cech
    63	representative of its relative Picard class, and refines that class to a basic-open datum.
    64	-/
    65	theorem nonempty
    66	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    67	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) :
    68	    Nonempty (PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam) := by
    69	  have hplus : ∀ a : PicEtAff C A,
    70	      ∃ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E),
    71	        PicEtAff.mk C E x = a := by
    72	    intro a
    73	    induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
    74	    | mk E x => exact ⟨E, x, rfl⟩
    75	  obtain ⟨E, x, hrep⟩ := hplus (picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)
    76	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k E.Carrier)
    77	    (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))
    78	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
    79	    (C := C) (B := E.Carrier) (π := pi) c
    80	  refine ⟨
    81	    { cover := E
    82	      representative := x
    83	      represents := hrep
    84	      datum := D
    85	      datum_class := ?_ }⟩
    86	  calc
    87	    (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
    88	        relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier) c := hc.symm
    89	    _ = relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier) D.cechPicClass :=
    90	      congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) hD.symm
    91	
    92	noncomputable local instance (priority := 20000) nativeDatumDegreeOver
    93	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    94	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
    95	  instOverBaseChange C L
    96	
    97	noncomputable local instance nativeDatumDegreeSmooth
    98	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    99	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   100	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   101	
   102	noncomputable local instance nativeDatumDegreeIntegral
   103	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   104	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
   105	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   106	
   107	noncomputable local instance nativeDatumDegreeQuasiCompact
   108	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   109	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   110	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   111	
   112	noncomputable local instance nativeDatumDegreeFiniteH0
   113	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   114	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   115	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   116	
   117	noncomputable local instance nativeDatumDegreeFiniteH1
   118	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   119	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   120	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   121	
   122	/-- The datum extracted from a genus-degree class has genus degree after every field-valued
   123	coefficient extension.
   124	
   125	This is forced by the two class-identification fields of `P`; it is not an additional rank-one
   126	hypothesis. -/
   127	theorem classDeg_baseChange
   128	    {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
   129	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   130	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
   131	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier L]
   132	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier L] :
   133	    classDeg L
   134	      (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   135	        P.datum.cechPicClass) = genus C :=
   136	  PicRankOneLocalPresentation.datum_classDeg_baseChange_of_representation
   137	    P.cover P.representative P.represents P.datum P.datum_class L
   138	
   139	/-- Split witnesses for the represented class on every residue field give the exact residue
   140	`H¹` witnesses for the same extracted datum.
   141	
   142	The proof first identifies the datum with its relative Picard representative, uses the existing
   143	pointwise presentation equivalence, and then transports across the canonical comparison between
   144	the scheme-theoretic and algebraic residue fields. -/
   145	theorem residueH1Witness_of_isSplitWitness
   146	    {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
   147	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   148	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
   149	    (hsplit : ∀ t : (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier).left,
   150	      IsSplitWitness C
   151	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
   152	          (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   153	            (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))))) :
   154	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier,
   155	      P.datum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
   156	  intro p
   157	  have hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C pi
   158	      (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   159	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) P.datum.cechPicClass))
   160	      P.datum :=
   161	    isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C pi
   162	      P.datum.cechPicClass P.datum rfl
   163	  have hpres := isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower C pi hfib
   164	  have hs : IsSplitWitness C
   165	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint
   166	        (show (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier).left from p))
   167	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   168	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) P.datum.cechPicClass))) := by
   169	    simpa only [← P.datum_class] using hsplit p
   170	  have hp : P.datum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing
   171	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) p) :=
   172	    (hpres p).mpr hs
   173	  letI : Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   174	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) p) :=
   175	    ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of P.cover.Carrier) p).inv).hom.toAlgebra
   176	  haveI : IsScalarTower P.cover.Carrier p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   177	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) p) :=
   178	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq'
   179	      (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors p)
   180	  exact (P.datum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
   181	    p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   182	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) p)).mpr hp
   183	
   184	end PicRankOneNativeDatum
   185	
   186	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# Field-extension stability for rank-one presentation witnesses
    11	
    12	The rank-one layer delivered by the translated-cover construction is a class over a field.
    13	Testing its pullback over an arbitrary affine algebra reads that class at residue fields, which
    14	are arbitrary extensions of the original field.  This file proves that the split-witness
    15	condition survives every such extension.
    16	
    17	The proof does not reuse the original splitting field directly.  If `N / K` is the finite
    18	separable splitting supplied by the witness and `L / K` is arbitrary, a field factor `P / L`
    19	of `L \otimes[K] N` is finite separable over `L` and receives `N`.  The presenting Cech class
    20	and its `H^1` witness are then transported from `N` to `P`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	open AlgebraicJacobian
    35	
    36	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    37	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    38	
    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    40	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    42	
    43	noncomputable section
    44	
    45	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
    46	-- Constructing and transporting through a field factor of `L ⊗[K] N` needs the larger budget.
    47	/-- A split witness remains a split witness after an arbitrary extension of its reading field.
    48	
    49	The output splitting field is not the original one: it is a finite-separable field factor of
    50	the base change of the original field cover.  Consequently no finiteness, separability, or
    51	algebraicity assumption is imposed on the reading-field extension itself.  The auxiliary finite
    52	map `pi` is used only to choose a basic-open cocycle datum through which the `H¹` witness is
    53	transported. -/
    54	theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_of_algHom
    55	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    56	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    57	    (e : K →ₐ[k] L) (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    58	    (h : IsSplitWitness C nu) :
    59	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e) nu) := by
    60	  obtain ⟨N, hNf, hkN, hKN, htowkKN, hNfin, hNsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
    61	  letI := hNf
    62	  letI := hkN
    63	  letI := hKN
    64	  letI := htowkKN
    65	  letI := hNfin
    66	  letI := hNsep
    67	  letI hKL : Algebra K L := e.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    68	  haveI htowkKL : IsScalarTower k K L :=
    69	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (e.commutes x).symm
    70	  obtain ⟨P, hPf, hLP, hPfin, hPsep, ⟨q⟩⟩ :=
    71	    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) N).baseChange L).exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
    72	  letI := hPf
    73	  letI := hLP
    74	  letI := hPfin
    75	  letI := hPsep
    76	  letI hkP : Algebra k P := ((algebraMap L P).comp (algebraMap k L)).toAlgebra
    77	  haveI htowkLP : IsScalarTower k L P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    78	  letI hKP : Algebra K P := ((algebraMap L P).comp e.toRingHom).toAlgebra
    79	  haveI htowKLP : IsScalarTower K L P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    80	  haveI htowkKP : IsScalarTower k K P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
    81	    change algebraMap L P (algebraMap k L x) = algebraMap L P (e (algebraMap k K x))
    82	    rw [e.commutes]
    83	  set sigma : N →ₐ[K] P :=
    84	    ((q.restrictScalars K).comp
    85	        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) N).baseChangeInclude L)).comp
    86	      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) N).symm.toAlgHom with hsigma
    87	  letI hNP : Algebra N P := sigma.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    88	  haveI htowKNP : IsScalarTower K N P :=
    89	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (sigma.commutes x).symm
    90	  haveI htowkNP : IsScalarTower k N P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
    91	    change algebraMap k P x = sigma (algebraMap k N x)
    92	    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k K N, sigma.commutes,
    93	      ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k K P]
    94	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ :=
    95	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := N) (π := pi) M
    96	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C N N) D.cechPicClass
    97	      = D.cechPicClass := by
    98	    have hmap : relCurveMap C N N = 𝟙 (relCurve C N) := by
    99	      rw [relCurveMap]
   100	      have hbase : overSpecMap (k := k) N N = 𝟙 (overSpec k N) :=
   101	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
   102	      rw [hbase, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
   103	      rfl
   104	    rw [hmap, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
   105	    rfl
   106	  have hWitnessN : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing N :=
   107	    ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
   108	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
   109	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension N P).mp hWitnessN
   110	  have hMP : PicEtAff.map C P (picEtAffineEquiv C K nu)
   111	      = PicEtAff.unit C P
   112	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k P) (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C N P) M)) := by
   113	    have hmap := congrArg (PicEtAff.map C P) hM
   114	    rw [PicEtAff.map_map, PicEtAff.map_unit, relPicAlgMap_mk] at hmap
   115	    exact hmap
   116	  refine isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness C _
   117	    (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C N P) M) ?_ W' ?_ hW1'
   118	  · rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
   119	    change PicEtAff.map C P (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K nu)) = _
   120	    rw [PicEtAff.map_map]
   121	    exact hMP
   122	  · rw [hW', hD]
   123	
   124	/-- A native datum for the arbitrary-affine pullback of a split field class has the required
   125	residue-field `H¹` witnesses.
   126	
   127	This is a field-origin specialization, not a claim for an arbitrary affine Picard class.  The
   128	map to each residue field factors through the affine algebra and the chosen etale cover, so the
   129	single split witness over `K` supplies all pointwise witnesses needed by the datum. -/
   130	theorem PicRankOneNativeDatum.residueH1Witness_of_fieldPullback
   131	    {K A : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   132	    {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
   133	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   134	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
   135	    (e : K →ₐ[k] A) (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   136	    (hlam : lam.1 = picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e) nu)
   137	    (hsplit : IsSplitWitness C nu) :
   138	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier,
   139	      P.datum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
   140	  apply P.residueH1Witness_of_isSplitWitness
   141	  intro t
   142	  let iota : A →ₐ[k] P.cover.Carrier :=
   143	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k
   144	  let rho : P.cover.Carrier →ₐ[k]
   145	      Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) t :=
   146	    IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier _
   147	  let phi : K →ₐ[k]
   148	      Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) t :=
   149	    rho.comp (iota.comp e)
   150	  have hcover :
   151	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 =
   152	        relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   153	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) :=
   154	    picEtMap_eq_relPicToPicEt_of_affineRepresentative
   155	      C lam.1 P.cover P.representative P.represents.symm
   156	  have hpoint : Over.testPoint t = Over.overSpecMap rho := by
   157	    rw [testPoint_eq_overSpecMap]
   158	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   159	    rfl
   160	  have hmaps :
   161	      (Over.testPoint t ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) ≫ Over.overSpecMap e =
   162	        Over.overSpecMap phi := by
   163	    rw [Category.assoc, hpoint, ← Over.overSpecMap_comp, ← Over.overSpecMap_comp]
   164	  have hclass :
   165	      picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
   166	          (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   167	            (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) =
   168	        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi) nu := by
   169	    calc
   170	      _ = picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
   171	          (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1) := by rw [hcover]
   172	      _ = picEtMap C
   173	          (Over.testPoint t ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 :=
   174	        (picEtMap_comp (C := C) (Over.overSpecMap iota)
   175	          (Over.testPoint t) lam.1).symm
   176	      _ = picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota)
   177	          (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e) nu) := by rw [hlam]
   178	      _ = picEtMap C
   179	          ((Over.testPoint t ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) ≫
   180	            Over.overSpecMap e) nu :=
   181	        (picEtMap_comp (C := C) (Over.overSpecMap e)
   182	          (Over.testPoint t ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) nu).symm
   183	      _ = picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi) nu :=
   184	        congrArg (fun f => picEtMap C f nu) hmaps
   185	  rw [hclass]
   186	  exact isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_of_algHom
   187	    (C := C) pi phi nu hsplit
   188	
   189	end

     8	/-!
     9	# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract
    10	
    11	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
    12	This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
    13	always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
    14	`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
    15	arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
    16	explicit obligations.
    17	
    18	The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
    19	second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
    21	through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    41	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    42	
    43	/-! ## The native adapter contract -/
    44	
    45	/--
    46	A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
    47	cocycle datum.
    48	
    49	The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
    50	certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
    51	calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
    52	evaluation module.
    53	-/
    54	structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    55	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    56	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    57	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    58	  represents :
    59	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    60	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    61	  datum_class :
    62	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    63	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    64	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    65	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    66	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    67	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    68	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    69	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    70	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
    71	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    72	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    73	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    74	  h0_rank_one :
    75	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    76	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    77	
    78	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    79	
    80	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    81	
    82	/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.
    83	
    84	The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
    85	without weakening or adding hypotheses.
    86	-/
    87	noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    88	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    89	    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
    90	  { cover := P.cover
    91	    representative := P.representative
    92	    represents := P.represents
    93	    datum := P.datum
    94	    datum_class := P.datum_class
    95	    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    96	    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    97	    line_bundle := P.datum.nativeModule_isLineBundle
    98	    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    99	    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
   100	    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
   101	    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
   102	    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }
   103	
   104	theorem nonempty_localPresentation
   105	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
   106	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
   107	  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩
   108	
   109	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
   110	
   111	/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/
   112	
   113	/--
   114	An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
   115	consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
   116	`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
   117	choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
   118	-/
   119	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
   120	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   121	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   122	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   123	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
   124	        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
   125	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
   126	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   127	  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
   128	  intro A _ _ t
   129	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
   130	  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation
   131	
   132	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# Lambda-tied assembly of rank-one family certificates
    12	
    13	This file is the Picard-side consumer of `RankOneFamilyCertificates`.  It does not choose a
    14	module: the certificate and the native presentation are both attached to the displayed cocycle
    15	datum.  The cover representative and its equality with the displayed lambda class provide the
    16	Picard tie, while arbitrary-cartesian native pushforward base change remains a separate geometric
    17	input.
    18	-/

    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    38	
    39	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    40	
    41	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    42	
    43	/-! ## The literal native consumer -/
    44	
    45	/-- Assemble the native presentation from certificates for the same displayed cocycle datum.
    46	
    47	The equalities `hrep` and `hclass` tie the datum to the requested lambda class.  All four
    48	cohomological fields are projected from `cert`, whose modules are definitionally the H-modules
    49	of `D.sheaf`; no unrelated or pre-certified target module can enter.  The all-cartesian native
    50	pushforward comparison is intentionally an explicit argument until its protected producer lands.
    51	-/
    52	noncomputable def ofCertificates
    53	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
    54	    (x : descentClasses C E)
    55	    (hrep : PicEtAff.mk C E x = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)
    56	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C E.Carrier pi)
    57	    (hclass :
    58	      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
    59	        relPicMk C (overSpec k E.Carrier) D.cechPicClass)
    60	    (hpush :
    61	      ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    62	        (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of E.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    63	        (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C E.Carrier)
    64	        (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    65	          (relCurve C E.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of E.Carrier)) g),
    66	        IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app D.nativeModule))
    67	    (cert : RankOneFamilyCertificates D) :
    68	    PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam :=
    69	  { cover := E
    70	    representative := x
    71	    represents := hrep
    72	    datum := D
    73	    datum_class := hclass
    74	    native_pushforward_base_change := hpush
    75	    h1_vanishing := cert.h1_vanishing
    76	    h0_finite := cert.h0_finite
    77	    h0_projective := cert.h0_projective
    78	    h0_rank_one := cert.h0_rank_one }
    79	
    80	end PicRankOneNativePresentation

    82	end AlgebraicGeometry

    12	/-!
    13	# Native rank-one certificates for the lambda-tied datum
    14	
    15	This file closes the Picard-side consumer boundary.  A `PicRankOneNativeDatum` already records
    16	that its etale representative presents the displayed lambda and that its basic-open cocycle datum
    17	represents that same relative Picard class.  Residue-field split witnesses therefore produce the
    18	four cohomological certificates for this exact datum over its arbitrary affine coefficient ring.
    19	
    20	The returned package uses the canonical `h0BaseChange` and `scalarExtension` operations from
    21	`RankOneFamilyCertificates`; `h0BaseChange_tower` proves their coherence along every affine
    22	coefficient tower.  The final constructor passes the package directly to
    23	`PicRankOneNativePresentation.ofCertificates`.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    28	
    29	universe u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    32	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    33

    36	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    37	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    38	
    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    40	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    42	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    43	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    44	variable {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    45	
    46	namespace PicRankOneNativeDatum
    47	
    48	/-- The pointwise split condition on the displayed lambda representative carried by `P`. -/
    49	abbrev ResidueSplitWitnesses (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam) : Prop :=
    50	  ∀ t : (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier).left,
    51	    IsSplitWitness C
    52	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
    53	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
    54	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))))
    55	
    56	/-- Produce the complete arbitrary-affine certificate package for the lambda-tied datum `P`.
    57	
    58	The H1 input is converted from split witnesses for `P.representative`; the degree law is derived
    59	from `P.represents` and `P.datum_class`.  Finiteness and projectivity are constructed at a genuine
    60	finite Noetherian stage and transported back, rather than supplied by the caller. -/
    61	noncomputable def familyCertificates
    62	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
    63	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    64	    (hsplit : P.ResidueSplitWitnesses) :
    65	    RankOneFamilyCertificates P.datum :=
    66	  RankOneFamilyCertificates.ofActualDatum P.datum hpi
    67	    (P.residueH1Witness_of_isSplitWitness hsplit)
    68	    (fun L ↦ P.classDeg_baseChange L)
    69	
    70	/-- Canonically extend the lambda-tied certificate package to any affine coefficient algebra. -/
    71	noncomputable def familyCertificatesBaseChange
    72	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
    73	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    74	    (hsplit : P.ResidueSplitWitnesses)
    75	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
    76	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
    77	    RankOneFamilyCertificates (P.datum.baseChange B) :=
    78	  (P.familyCertificates hpi hsplit).scalarExtension B
    79	
    80	end PicRankOneNativeDatum
    81	
    82	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    83	
    84	/-- Assemble a native rank-one presentation from the actual lambda-tied datum and its split
    85	witnesses.  The only remaining independent input is the native pushforward base-change theorem. -/
    86	noncomputable def ofNativeDatum
    87	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
    88	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    89	    (hsplit : P.ResidueSplitWitnesses)
    90	    (hpush :
    91	      ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    92	        (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    93	        (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
    94	        (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    95	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g),
    96	        IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.datum.nativeModule)) :
    97	    PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam :=
    98	  PicRankOneNativePresentation.ofCertificates
    99	    P.cover P.representative P.represents P.datum P.datum_class hpush
   100	      (P.familyCertificates hpi hsplit)
   101	
   102	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
   103	
   104	end AlgebraicGeometry
